_metadata.description: Drug class reference for CareCue conflict detection. Cross-checked against WHO ATC classification and NIH RxClass. Scoped to medications relevant to elderly care and commonly available in India.

statin.label: Statins (Cholesterol)
statin.description: Lower cholesterol by blocking liver enzyme. Taking two statins together increases risk of muscle side effects.
statin.source: WHO ATC C10AA / RxClass Pharmacologic: HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitors

ace_inhibitor.label: ACE Inhibitors (Blood Pressure)
ace_inhibitor.description: Lower blood pressure by relaxing blood vessels. Taking two ACE inhibitors together can cause dangerously low blood pressure and kidney problems.
ace_inhibitor.source: WHO ATC C09AA / RxClass Pharmacologic: ACE Inhibitors

arb.label: ARBs (Blood Pressure)
arb.description: Lower blood pressure by blocking a chemical that tightens blood vessels. Taking two ARBs together or with an ACE inhibitor increases kidney risk.
arb.source: WHO ATC C09CA / RxClass Pharmacologic: Angiotensin II Receptor Blockers

ace_inhibitor_or_arb.label: ACE Inhibitors and ARBs (Blood Pressure)
ace_inhibitor_or_arb.description: Both ACE inhibitors and ARBs lower blood pressure through related pathways. Combining them increases risk of kidney problems and high potassium.
ace_inhibitor_or_arb.source: WHO ATC C09 / RxClass Pharmacologic: Renin-Angiotensin System

beta_blocker.label: Beta Blockers (Heart/Blood Pressure)
beta_blocker.description: Slow heart rate and lower blood pressure. Taking multiple beta blockers together can cause dangerously slow heart rate and low blood pressure.
beta_blocker.source: WHO ATC C07AA+C07AB+C07AG / RxClass Pharmacologic: Beta Adrenergic Blockers

diuretic.label: Diuretics (Water Pills)
diuretic.description: Help the body remove excess water and salt. Combining different diuretics or with ACE inhibitors/ARBs can cause dehydration and electrolyte problems.
diuretic.source: WHO ATC C03 / RxClass Pharmacologic: Diuretics

calcium_channel_blocker.label: Calcium Channel Blockers (Blood Pressure)
calcium_channel_blocker.description: Lower blood pressure by relaxing blood vessel walls. Combining with beta blockers can cause heart rhythm problems.
calcium_channel_blocker.source: WHO ATC C08CA / RxClass Pharmacologic: Calcium Channel Blocking Agents

thiazide_diuretic.label: Thiazide Diuretics (Water Pills)
thiazide_diuretic.description: A specific type of water pill. Combining with other diuretics can cause electrolyte imbalances.
thiazide_diuretic.source: WHO ATC C03AA / RxClass Pharmacologic: Thiazides

loop_diuretic.label: Loop Diuretics (Strong Water Pills)
loop_diuretic.description: Stronger water pills used for fluid retention. Combining with thiazides or ACE inhibitors/ARBs can cause dehydration.
loop_diuretic.source: WHO ATC C03C / RxClass Pharmacologic: Loop Diuretics

anticoagulant.label: Blood Thinners (Anticoagulants)
anticoagulant.description: Prevent blood clots. Combining multiple blood thinners greatly increases bleeding risk.
anticoagulant.source: WHO ATC B01AA / RxClass Pharmacologic: Vitamin K Antagonists

antiplatelet.label: Platelet Blockers (Antiplatelet)
antiplatelet.description: Prevent blood clots by stopping platelets from sticking together. Combining two antiplatelets or with anticoagulants increases bleeding risk.
antiplatelet.source: WHO ATC B01AC / RxClass Pharmacologic: Platelet Aggregation Inhibitors

anticoagulant_or_antiplatelet.label: Blood Thinners (Anticoagulants and Antiplatelets)
anticoagulant_or_antiplatelet.description: All blood-thinning medications. Combining any of these significantly increases bleeding risk.
anticoagulant_or_antiplatelet.source: WHO ATC B01 / RxClass Pharmacologic: Antithrombotic Agents

thyroid_hormone.label: Thyroid Hormones
thyroid_hormone.description: Replace or supplement thyroid hormone. Taking two thyroid hormones together can cause hyperthyroid symptoms.
thyroid_hormone.source: WHO ATC H03AA / RxClass Pharmacologic: Thyroid Hormones

proton_pump_inhibitor.label: Proton Pump Inhibitors (Stomach Acid Reducers)
proton_pump_inhibitor.description: Reduce stomach acid. Taking two PPIs together provides no added benefit and may increase side effects.
proton_pump_inhibitor.source: WHO ATC A02BC / RxClass Pharmacologic: Proton Pump Inhibitors

biguanide.label: Biguanides (Diabetes - Metformin)
biguanide.description: Lower blood sugar by reducing liver glucose production. Taking two biguanides increases risk of lactic acidosis.
biguanide.source: WHO ATC A10BA / RxClass Pharmacologic: Biguanides

sulfonylurea.label: Sulfonylureas (Diabetes - Insulin Stimulators)
sulfonylurea.description: Lower blood sugar by making the pancreas produce more insulin. Taking two sulfonylureas together increases hypoglycemia risk.
sulfonylurea.source: WHO ATC A10BB / RxClass Pharmacologic: Sulfonylureas

antidiabetic.label: Diabetes Medicines (All Oral)
antidiabetic.description: All oral diabetes medications. Combining multiple classes can increase hypoglycemia risk.
antidiabetic.source: WHO ATC A10B / RxClass Pharmacologic: Blood Glucose Lowering Drugs

levodopa.label: Levodopa (Parkinson's)
levodopa.description: Replace dopamine in the brain for Parkinson's disease. Taking two levodopa combinations can worsen side effects.
levodopa.source: WHO ATC N04BA / RxClass Pharmacologic: Dopamine Agonists
